title: Unearthed: Tracing Responsible Gold ft Dr Robin Kolvenbach, Argor-Heraeus
gist: Podcast episode summary (thin, promotional): WGC's John Reade and Joe Cavatoni speak with Argor-Heraeus CEO Dr Robin Kolvenbach about responsible gold sourcing as a strategic opportunity, the Small Craft premium returned to ASGM communities, and how the WGC's London Gold Principles could scale such practices industry-wide. Despite the record's 'central bank demand' category, the text contains no central-bank content.

insights.claim: Argor-Heraeus, a major Swiss precious metals refiner in Mendrisio, treats responsible gold sourcing as a strategic opportunity rather than a compliance burden.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Refiners positioning sourcing standards as a commercial differentiator may command premium relationships with downstream buyers.
insights.quote: treats responsible sourcing as a strategic opportunity rather than a compliance burden

insights.claim: Argor-Heraeus's downstream-focused business model is presented as reinforcing its compliance standards, because proximity to end customers raises the bar on provenance.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Vertical integration toward end users can be a structural driver of stricter supply-chain due diligence in gold refining.
insights.quote: why the company's downstream-focused business model reinforces its compliance standards

insights.claim: Argor-Heraeus has stated an ambition to become the world's most responsible gold refiner, backed by a sizeable dedicated team.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Signals rising competition among Swiss refiners on traceability credentials, a factor in sourcing and bar acceptance.
insights.quote: its ambition to become the world's most responsible gold refiner

insights.claim: Argor-Heraeus's Small Craft product channels a small premium directly back into artisanal and small-scale gold mining (ASGM) communities.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Shows a premium-pricing model for traceable ASGM gold, a potential template for monetising provenance.
insights.quote: Small Craft product, which channels a small premium directly back into ASGM communities

insights.claim: Responsible sourcing from artisanal and small-scale gold mining is scaling, and the discussion identifies where it is scaling fastest (regions not named in the episode summary).
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Formalisation of ASGM supply could gradually bring more traceable artisanal gold into the regulated market.
insights.quote: where responsible ASGM sourcing is scaling fastest

insights.claim: The World Gold Council's London Gold Principles are framed as a vehicle that could take refiner-level responsible sourcing efforts industry-wide.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Industry-wide sourcing standards could reshape which gold is acceptable in the London market and raise compliance costs for laggards.
insights.quote: how the World Gold Council's London Gold Principles could take these efforts industry-wide
